summary: 58-year-old man on diclofenac for osteoarthritis and aspirin 75 mg for secondary prevention: 6 weeks of epigastric pain; OGD shows a 1 cm benign-looking antral ulcer, CLO negative, biopsies taken. Stop the NSAID, full-dose PPI 8 weeks, repeat OGD for gastric ulcer; aspirin decision stays with the clinician.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Upper abdominal pain — review after endoscopy
inputs.hpi: Six weeks of gnawing epigastric pain, worse after food. Takes diclofenac 50 mg three times daily for knee osteoarthritis and aspirin 75 mg since a TIA two years ago. OGD last week: 1 cm clean-based antral gastric ulcer, benign appearance, biopsies taken, rapid urease test negative. No bleeding, weight steady.

imaging.name: OGD
imaging.result: 1 cm clean-based gastric antral ulcer, benign appearance (Forrest III). Biopsies from ulcer edge taken. Rapid urease test negative.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: NSAID-associated gastric ulcer
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Uncomplicated NSAID-associated gastric antral ulcer (no bleeding), H. pylori rapid urease negative, biopsies pending. On diclofenac and low-dose aspirin (secondary prevention after TIA).

redFlags.note: Continuing the NSAID risks bleeding or perforation.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Emergency now (score 52): adaptiveTriage reads CC+HPI free text without negation — "No bleeding" matches the "GI or other bleeding" urgent red flag; exam "no peritonism" also fires the "Generalised peritonism" safety prompt.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Negation handling in adaptive-triage and computeClinicalPrompts exam-text rules.

mustInclude.note: A negative rapid urease test on PPI/NSAID may be false-negative; confirm with histology or breath/stool test.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: peptic_ulcer protocol gives omeprazole 20 mg OD "4–8 weeks" in medications (matched only in part) — the plan text has no 8-week full-dose course for an NSAID ulcer.

mustExclude.note: Aspirin for secondary prevention after TIA is continued with PPI cover; stopping it is a clinician decision, never an automatic plan line.

guideline.name: NICE CG184 — Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and dyspepsia in adults: investigation and management
guideline.section: NSAID-associated peptic ulcer: stop the NSAID where possible; full-dose PPI or H2RA for 8 weeks; test for H. pylori; repeat endoscopy 6–8 weeks after treatment for gastric ulcer; low-dose aspirin continued with gastroprotection when indicated
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG184. London: NICE; 2014 (last updated 2019).

guideline.name: Maastricht VI/Florence consensus report — management of Helicobacter pylori infection
guideline.section: Test for H. pylori in peptic ulcer disease; rapid urease test sensitivity reduced by PPI
guideline.citation: Malfertheiner P, Megraud F, Rokkas T, et al. Gut. 2022;71:1724–1762.

rationale: Uncomplicated NSAID ulcer with low-dose aspirin for secondary prevention. The NSAID must stop; the aspirin must not be stopped by a template. Also checks that an uncomplicated ulcer is not treated as a bleed by the web variant logic.
